content.comment_body: Hello everyone, this is my first post here and my English isn’t very strong. I have a [product_name] with [article_no], and when I connect it to 220VAC, it only shows a loading screen and nothing else happens. Is my device possibly broken? How can I fix this issue?

My English isn’t great either. The loading sequence lasts about 20 seconds, after which the [product_name] should start. If it doesn’t, unfortunately your device may have failed. I’ve used many [product_name] devices and haven’t encountered this problem before. Good luck!

Thank you very much! I’ve tried waiting 20 seconds multiple times, but nothing changes. Sometimes the loading animation flashes or fades, and occasionally the menu appears briefly before disappearing. Is it possible to reprogram the device? Could I somehow flash the ARM processor to make it work again?

Hi, please verify your power supply to ensure it meets specifications and isn’t introducing electrical noise. A faulty power supply could be the issue. Also, you cannot reprogram this specific [product_name] as you described. Hope this information helps.
Thanks for your help. I’m considering trying 12 or 24VDC instead of 220VAC to see if that solves the problem. Also, could you explain what EMV means?

Hello, EMV typically refers to Europay, MasterCard, and Visa, but in this context it’s likely meant to be EMC (electromagnetic compatibility), which deals mostly with grounding problems. If your PC is connected to the [product_name] powered by 230V and either the PC or the device isn’t properly grounded, this can cause sparks at the programming interface and potentially damage the device.
Thanks a lot! How can you repair a [product_name] that has been damaged by a spark at the programming interface?
Hi, usually the solution is to replace it with a functioning unit.

Hello, your [product_name] only operates on 115 to 240VAC, so using 12 or 24VDC won’t work. If you purchased a new device, contact [company_name] support for assistance—they might be able to help if the device was supplied with a fault.

Hi, thanks for your response. I’m facing a new issue: the last time I used my device, it overheated, and when I turned it off and back on, it wouldn’t power up. I found that the SMD fuse with a value of zero burned out. The device appears to be completely dead now. I couldn’t locate any service manuals online—do you have any advice on how to fix this?

Hello, there aren’t any official service manuals available online. Did anything specific cause your device to get hot? That burned part might be a zero-ohm resistor acting as a wire bridge or fuse. If components have burned, usually there is more damage elsewhere. In cases like this, repair generally isn’t worthwhile, but if this is a hobby project, you can try swapping the damaged part and see if it works again.

I didn’t do anything that could have caused overheating—the device was operating normally before it got hot. After opening the case, I saw a burned zero-ohm resistor but all other parts looked fine. I tried rewiring the circuit with no success. When testing the connection between the power and main board, I measured 70VDC on one pin and even saw a spark on the same pin after reconnecting. Since [product_name] devices are quite expensive where I live, I’d prefer to repair it rather than buy a new one, but I’m not sure how to proceed. Thank you!
Double-check all your connections—there may be a short circuit in your wiring.
Hello, I think a short circuit on the device’s electronic board caused the overheating. You can try to repair it, but replacing it with a new one might be better.

Hello, for hardware problems or faulty supply, you should contact [company_name] support for help. If the warranty is void due to damage, you might look for a local [company_name] product repair specialist to repair your device.

analysis.insight_summary: The main user describes persistent boot issues with a [product_name] after power-up, where only the loading animation is shown and the menu appears briefly, suggesting hardware damage—likely from a bad power supply or electrical spark during programming interface connection. Others confirm this malfunction is uncommon, and recovery options are very limited. The user’s attempts at different voltages and discovery of a burnt fuse indicate severe hardware failure.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] to start up reliably and display the standard menu. They hope the device can be repaired, whether by reprogramming or simply replacing basic components like fuses, and wish to find service manuals and repair resources.
